rules.body: Apply when deferred edits belong to a persistent document resource while its visible observer has a shorter lifetime, and saves may synchronously reenter navigation. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously."

Push workspace edits into the existing document-specific trailing task, replacing pending text and restarting its quiet interval. After 120 ms of quiet, write the latest text exactly once; keep the task reusable for later bursts. Evidence: TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save."

Keep buffers owned by the store and keyed by document ID; retiring a badge must remove its subscription without discarding the document's pending edit. Flush pending departing-document work before open, close, or dispose returns. Evidence: README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge." TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." The original src/workflow.go persists edits synchronously: "func(w *Workspace)Edit(text string){view:=w.current;if view!=nil{w.env.Write(view.id,text)}}"

Clear pending task state before invoking callback-capable work, preserving reuse and preventing a nested flush from repeating the same edit. Retain the existing ordering in src/workflow.go: "text:=t.pending;t.handle=nil;t.pending=nil" followed by "if text!=nil { t.work(*text) }".

Treat departure saving as a synchronous reentry boundary. Capture and clear the departing view, complete its subscription cleanup and departure output before flushing, and avoid further unconditional view mutations after flushing. An outer open must verify its navigation generation after departure work before installing a view, so newer callback-driven navigation remains authoritative. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." The original src/workflow.go already guards installation with "request!=w.generation{return}".

Preserve document identity, valid empty text, revision/status payload construction, and live subscription behavior while changing edit timing. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Verify that an empty pending string is saved rather than treated as absence of work.

Do not transfer document departure persistence to the transient preview. Preserve its 40 ms task, cancellation on hide, and later reuse. Evidence: TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/workflow.go: "func NewPreview(env Environment)*Preview{return &Preview{NewTrailing(env,40,func(query string){env.Output(\"preview\",Value{\"query\":query})})}}" and "func(p *Preview)Hide(){p.task.Cancel()}".

Verify no write before the 120 ms quiet boundary, one latest-text write afterward, and another successful later burst. Check pending edits across open, close, dispose, and reopening; check synchronous save callbacks that open or close a view; check subscription cleanup and unchanged payloads. Separately verify preview timing, discard on hide, and reuse. These checks operationalize the cited TASK and public source requirements; evaluation outcomes do not expand their scope.

limitations: Departure flushing follows from preserving previously synchronous persistence together with store-owned document buffers; TASK does not explicitly state a new departure timing requirement.
The Environment interface does not establish whether cancellation prevents an already-dispatched timer callback; no stronger timer guarantee is inferred.
Attempt 1 passed the supplied observations, but those observations neither create requirements nor establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit across tasks.
No concurrent-access or additional error-handling requirements are specified by the supplied public sources.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
